title: podlake load: high memory + slow on large loads (wide MARC schema)
description:
Observed while testing: `podlake load` of ~2M Brown records used ~8 GB RAM (~20% on the test box) and took a good chunk of time. Not even a large set.

## Likely root cause
The marctable schema is extremely wide — hundreds/~1000 all-VARCHAR columns (a column per MARC field tag and every field+subfield combo), mostly null. 2M rows x ~1000 columns ~= ~2B cells, which DuckDB buffers into row groups and rewrites as partitioned, snappy-compressed DuckLake Parquet during INSERT ... FROM read_parquet(). DuckDB's default memory_limit is ~80% of system RAM, so it uses a lot when available (8 GB was well under that cap, so it's not even memory-bound). Largely expected given the schema, but worth reducing.

## Investigate / options
- Set PRAGMA memory_limit and/or threads in lake.connect() to cap RAM.
- Batched inserts (chunk the read_parquet -> insert) instead of one large INSERT.
- Revisit the schema: drop all-null columns, or use a narrower/typed schema instead of ~1000 sparse VARCHAR columns.
- Note: the same wide-schema cost also drives the convert --batch-size memory (already exposed as a flag).
- Applies regardless of OAI vs ResourceSync ingestion.

## Files
- src/podlake/lake.py (load_parquet, _insert_parquet, connect)
- src/podlake/convert.py (_make_columns)
